conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.3 and the scaled number is -1.4 (p_up 45, abs_move 14). They agree. A low Q3 bar that Klarna has beaten at the top of its range in each of the last three quarters is offset by outside pressure on the Q4/FY guide, which is the line this stock has traded on at every print: the dollar strengthened after the August guide, German retail was weak through Q3, and Affirm's credit ticked up. Beats have been sold (-27% on Q4'25, -22% on Q2'26 with the guide cut), which keeps the beat finding small. A short book near 10% of float keeps p_up off the floor.
bar: Company Q3 guide: revenue $940-980m, GMV $35-36bn, TMD $340-360m, adjusted operating income $5-15m (Q2 2026 press release, 2026-08-18, https://s205.q4cdn.com/644747736/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/Q2-26-Klarna-Group-plc-Press-Release.pdf). Revenue consensus: $963.9m per Benzinga, $972.6m per Investing.com, $983m per another aggregator. EPS consensus -$0.13 to -$0.15 (Benzinga, TipRanks, Investing). Search summary: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/KLAR/earnings-forecasts and https://www.investing.com/equities/klarna-earnings. Consensus sits at or slightly above the guide midpoint. FY2026 guide: GMV $149-151bn, revenue $4.08-4.16bn, TMD $1.62-1.65bn, AOI $280-300m. With H1 AOI at $159m and Q3 guided at $5-15m, Q4 AOI must come in at $106-136m. Pre-cut consensus had FY revenue at $4.415bn. The bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources that roughly agree, so sizes are not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest: 36.8M shares, 9.7% of float, 5.9 days to cover at the 2026-10-06 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/klar/shortinterest); 37.49M shares, 7.6 days to cover at 2026-10-15 (https://massive.com/quote/klar). The level is elevated but below the 18-23% float that squeezed in the lessons file. Baseline skew is +2.55 vol points (mild downside paid) and put/call OI is 1.43. Heavy put flow was flagged on 2026-11-12 (TheFly, via the stockanalysis news list). Spot $13.74 is -60.6% from the 52-week high and +12% above the 52-week low. Run-up is +2.1% over 5 days and +5.1% over 20. Event-implied move is 12.97%. The realised earnings reactions, rebuilt by hand because the baseline's 6-K history mixes in non-earnings filings: Nov 2025 Q3 -9% intraday / about -3% close; 2026-02-19 Q4 about -27% close; 2026-05-14 Q1 about +20%; 2026-08-18 Q2 about -22%. Each one turned on the next-quarter or full-year guide.

findings.finding: Klarna has printed revenue at or above the top of its own quarterly guide three quarters running: Q4'25 $1.082bn vs a $1.065-1.08bn guide, Q1'26 about $1.0bn vs $900-980m, Q2'26 $1.042bn vs $960-1000m. Q2 included a $69m gain on a receivables sale. The Q3 guide is $940-980m, with consensus at $964-983m, so a repeat lands about $990-1000m, roughly 1-3% above consensus. That is a reported-quarter beat inside the company's own pattern.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats get sold. Q3'25 beat consensus ($903m vs $882m): -9% intraday. Q4'25 beat its own guide top: -27% on the Q1 guide. Q2'26 beat its guide top: about -22% on the FY cut. Only Q1'26 (+20%) paid, and there the FY framework was reaffirmed.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: consensus already sits above the guide midpoint. If the market expected a bigger beat, consensus would sit above $1bn. What is left is the gap between a top-of-range print and a mid-range consensus.
findings.independence: Guide history from other documents. Q2 guide $960m-$1bn: https://www.sherwood.news/markets/klarna-surges-on-1-billion-in-q1-revenue-and-user-growth/ (2026-05-14). Q1 guide $900-980m and Q4'25 actual $1.082bn: https://www.aol.com/articles/stock-market-today-feb-19-223707514.html. Q4'25 guide $1.065-1.08bn: https://www.tikr.com/blog/klarna-stock-sinks-over-9-despite-beating-consensus-estimates-in-q3

findings.finding: The dollar strengthened after the August 18 FY guide. EUR/USD fell more than 3% from its August high-week close of about 1.168 to about 1.135 by late September (StoneX, 2026-09-28). Reuters had the dollar up about 2.5% against the euro in September alone and heading for a third straight quarterly rise. The FY GMV guide of $149-151bn was cut in August partly for roughly $600m of FX translation. A further ~3% move on the non-US majority of a ~$43bn Q4 puts roughly $0.5-0.8bn of extra GMV translation headwind on the low end of that range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August FY GMV cut, which cited about $600m of FX, coincided with a -22% day. The Feb 2026 guide shortfall coincided with -27%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side FY GMV figures are anchored to the company's August range. A market that had priced a further FX cut would show consensus FY GMV below $149bn or a pre-print drift lower; instead the stock is up 5% over 20 days. The current November EUR/USD level is unverified, so the size is held small.
findings.independence: Reuters via bdnews24 (2026-09-30): dollar up nearly 2.5% vs euro in September, third straight quarterly rise, https://bdnews24.com/economy/5e41xplggt. The company itself named FX translation as a GMV guide driver: https://s205.q4cdn.com/644747736/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/earnings-result/Q2-26-Klarna-Group-plc-Press-Release.pdf

findings.finding: German retail was weak through Q3 2026, and Germany is Klarna's largest market by volume. Destatis: real retail sales -3.4% m/m in July. Secondary reports: September -2.0% m/m against a +0.4% forecast, -2.3% y/y, online/mail-order -2.2% m/m. Klarna already took a 'more measured view of primarily German volumes' in the August guide, so only a further deterioration is new.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August guide cut, which cited German volumes and FX, coincided with about -22%.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro series is public, but the transmission to Klarna's German GMV is not confirmed by the company. It is a proxy, partly inside the August guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: September print via tradingeconomics: https://tradingeconomics.com/germany/retail-sales/news/597168. Company caveat on German volumes in the Q2 press release (same document as the bar). This is a proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: US BNPL demand read-across is positive. Affirm reported 2026-11-05: GMV +34% y/y in the September quarter, early-FQ2 trends in the high-30s, and the FY27 GMV outlook raised to more than $65.25bn from more than $64bn. Klarna's US GMV grew 27% in Q2 and the US is its fastest-growing large region, with US assumptions unchanged in the August guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Klarna's US growth headline (+27-51%) has not prevented the large down-days on guide cuts. US strength alone has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print after Klarna last spoke. KLAR is up only 5% over 20 days and sits near its 52-week low, so no US-strength rerating is visible. The offset: Affirm's own stock fell after the print, so the market discounted the same data.
findings.independence: Shares the Affirm document with the credit finding below. Second source on GMV and the raised guide: https://www.tikr.com/blog/affirms-levchin-calls-30-plus-growth-the-floor-gmv-just-grew-34

findings.finding: US BNPL credit read-across is negative. Affirm's 30+ day delinquency, ex-Peloton, rose 35bp q/q to 2.9%, provisions grew 59% against 38% loan growth, and the stock sold off about 5-8%. Klarna's Q2 had provisions at 0.52% of GMV and US Fair Financing 30+ DPD down 20bp q/q. Klarna is also growing longer-duration US Fair Financing, which is the product most exposed to a turn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: credit provisions on Fair Financing were cited as a driver of the -27% day (https://paymentsindustryintelligence.com/?p=58851).
findings.why_not_priced: Klarna's move to fair-value accounting for new US/German Fair Financing nets provisions out of transaction costs, so the provision line is harder to read. Sector credit data landed after Klarna last spoke. Put/call OI of 1.43 and +2.55 skew suggest downside is partly bought already.
findings.independence: Shares the Affirm print with the demand finding. Second source on the 35bp delinquency rise: https://www.panabee.com/news/affirm-earnings-q1-2027 (AI-generated page, flagged). Sector surveys on rising BNPL late payments: https://www.digitaltransactions.net/?p=1330210

findings.finding: The FY AOI guide of $280-300m less H1 $159m and Q3's guided $5-15m requires Q4 adjusted operating income of $106-136m. That would be a record quarter, above Q2's $91m, and it follows a Q3 of heavy PSP-launch marketing spend. The Q4 holiday hockey stick is the line most exposed to a trim when the Q4 guide is given tomorrow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 guide below consensus: -27% (Feb). FY cut: -22% (Aug). FY reaffirmed: +20% (May).
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public and inside what the company guided, so most of it is known. What is not known is whether the Q3 launch spend has delivered the volume, and no source after August speaks to that.
findings.independence: The same primary document as the bar. The ts2.tech headline 'Outlook Points to 42% of Profit in Holiday Quarter' makes the same calculation (page gone, 410).

findings.finding: On 2026-11-12 Klarna named Chris Koegel, reported as a Robinhood executive, as CFO effective 2027-01-01. This resolves the open succession: CFO Neglén leaves for Adyen on 2027-02-01. The stock closed -5.6% that day at $12.71, then rose about 8% on 2026-11-13 per Benzinga's 'Why Is Klarna Stock Surging Friday'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August announcement of the CFO/CMO departures coincided with the -22% guide-cut day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the +8% Friday move is the market pricing it. The residual is that a US-facing CFO may present the guide differently on the call.

findings.finding: Short interest is about 37M shares, 9.7% of float, with 5.9-7.6 days to cover (October settlements). The stock is 60% off its high and 12% above its 52-week low, and put/call OI is 1.43. Any held or raised Q4/FY guide meets a short base that takes about a week to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026, FY framework reaffirmed: +20%. March 2026, chairman's $50m buy: +9%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It is an asymmetry mechanism on the upside tail, and it is why the negatives above are not sized larger.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first full quarter with new US and German Fair Financing booked at fair value. The company says this lowers reported revenue by about 10bp of GMV (about $35m a quarter), adds about 2bp of timing benefit to transaction margin, and moves provisions out of transaction costs. Some aggregators still carry a pre-guide Q3 revenue estimate of $1.108bn, so a headline 'revenue miss' against a stale number is possible even on a guide-top print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: day-one Fair Financing provisions were cited as a cause of the -27% day. The new presentation has not yet been tested by a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide includes it, so the effect is presentational. The risk is headline and algo comparison against a stale $1.108bn. If every estimate had updated, no source would still show $1.108bn.
findings.independence: The stale $1.108bn estimate appears in a search summary of https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/KLAR/estimates (page 403). Shares the press release with the bar and the Q4 AOI finding.

findings.finding: The Q2 revenue beat ($1.042bn vs a $960m-$1bn guide) included a $69m gain on the sale of consumer receivables. Without it, Q2 revenue was about $973m, inside the guide. The quality of the guide-top streak is lower than the headline suggests, and the Q3 comparison may not repeat the gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print fell about 22%. That move was attributed to the guide cut, not to beat quality.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly known. It tempers the beat finding above rather than standing as a strong negative.
findings.independence: Same RTTNews article as the beat finding. It is that finding's caveat, filed apart because it lands on beat quality.

outside_window.finding: On 2026-07-01 the Stockholm Patent and Market Court awarded PriceRunner (Klarna Technologies AB) about EUR1.3bn, roughly $1.97bn with interest, against Google. Google is appealing, leave is required, payment could take years, and the award is reduced by tax and by funder and former-shareholder arrangements. Under IFRS it is a contingent asset and is not expected in Q3 numbers.
